input.question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?
input.ground_truth: Most short lived coasters tend to have significant g forces that put extra stress on the structure. This causes harder wear on the rails, substructure, and train components. If the coaster has a unique or complex mechanism (tilt coasters, original LIM, launchers, etc) it will most likely have life span issues due to those components failing more and more with age.

Question: why do some roller coasters exhaust their lifespan in 8-10 years while others made of the same materials last 40+ at the same parks?

response.prediction:
Okay, imagine you have two toy cars made from the same plastic. One you play with every single day, zooming it down a big ramp over and over. The other toy car you only play with once in a while, and you keep it on a shelf most of the time.

The toy car you play with every day will get worn out faster, right? Its wheels might break, the paint might chip, and it might not work as well after a while. But the toy car you hardly play with will still look almost new after a long time!

Roller coasters are a bit like that. Some roller coasters are really popular and lots and lots of people ride them every single day. All that riding makes the parts move and wear out faster, just like your toy car. 

Other roller coasters might not be as popular, or maybe the park doesn’t let as many people ride them each day. So, those coasters don’t get used as much, and their parts don’t wear out as quickly.

Even if they’re made of the same stuff, using them a lot makes them get tired and need to be replaced sooner. That’s why some roller coasters don’t last as long as others, even if they’re made the same way!
